description:
Search live job postings advertised on JobJump, a German job board. Use this when the user wants to find open positions – by occupation, region, work mode, or contract type – or wants to know how many postings exist for a role in a place. Results are ordered by recency and by how well the title and region match the query; ordering is never influenced by what an employer pays JobJump, and the tool returns no advertising or sponsorship fields. JobJump covers Germany only.

Pass the user's own words for the occupation in `query` and, only if the user named a place to search in, that place in `search_region`. Do not infer `search_region` from device or client context, and never pass coordinates or a street address. To list one employer's postings, pass the `employer_slug` from get_top_employers in `employer`; an unknown slug returns NOT_FOUND. At least one of `query`, `search_region`, `category` or `employer` is required, because an unfiltered scan of the whole board is not useful.

Each result carries a stable job id, a canonical jobjump.net URL, a coarse location label, the employer's logo on JobJump's CDN when there is one, and a short plain-text excerpt of the employer's own advert. Salary appears only when the employer stated one; a separate `salary_estimate` field carries JobJump's own model estimate and is clearly marked as such. The tool does not return the employer's own apply URL, exact coordinates, contact people, or the full advert text – call get_job with a job id for the full description.

For more results, pass the returned `next_cursor` back unchanged together with identical filters; changing a filter invalidates the cursor. A cursor is valid for 15 minutes and paging stops after 100 records – narrow the query instead of paging further.

category.description: Occupational field, as one of JobJump's 17 fixed category slugs.

cursor.description: Opaque continuation token from a previous call's next_cursor. Pass it back unchanged with identical filters. Valid for 15 minutes.

employer.description: Restrict to one employer: the employer_slug from get_top_employers, or the part after 'bei-' in a jobjump.net/jobs URL. Matches the employer's postings under every spelling JobJump groups under it, including its brands' stores. Never guess a slug; call get_top_employers to find it.

home_office.description: Restrict to postings that allow working from home at least part of the time.

job_type.description: Contract or entry type, as one of JobJump's 7 fixed slugs, e.g. 'ausbildung' for an apprenticeship.

limit.description: Maximum number of postings to return. The server may return fewer.

posted_within_days.description: Only postings first published within this many days.

query.description: Occupation or job title in the user's own words, German or English. Gendered German forms are normalised, e.g. 'Erzieherin' also matches 'Erzieher'.

radius_km.description: How far around the resolved region to search, in kilometres. Only applies when search_region resolves to a place with a known centre. 0 means the named place only.

remote_only.description: Restrict to postings the employer marked as fully remote.

search_region.description: A place the user themselves named as a search criterion: a city, district or state in Germany. Free text. This is a search filter, not the user's location: never infer it, never fill it from device context, and never pass coordinates or an address.

name: search_jobs

logo_url.description: The employer logo JobJump shows on this posting, served from JobJump's CDN, or null when there is none on the CDN.

postings_series_id.description: Provenance entry of the postings in this response.

as_of.description: Vintage or reference period as published: 'YYYY', 'YYYY-MM' or an ISO date.

basis.description: Whether amounts are gross, net, or not a money amount.

dataset.description: Name of the dataset, e.g. 'Entgeltatlas' or 'JobJump salary aggregate'.

estimated.description: True when JobJump modelled or derived the value rather than observing or receiving it.

label.description: Short English name of what this series measures.

license.description: Licence or terms of use that apply to redistributing this series.

methodology_url.description: Public page describing how the series is produced, or null.

population.description: Who or what is counted, e.g. 'full-time employees subject to social insurance'.

sample_size.description: Number of underlying observations where JobJump knows it, otherwise null.

series_id.description: Stable key that series and values in this response refer to.

statistic.description: The statistic these values are. Read this before calling a value a median, a percentile or a maximum.

unit.description: Unit of every value carrying this series_id.

ags.description: Official German Kreis key (AGS) when one applies, otherwise null. Public administrative code, not a coordinate.

kind.description: Granularity the free-text input resolved to.

label.description: Coarse public name of the resolved region.

matched_input.description: The search_region text this resolution came from, echoed back so the user can see what was interpreted.

title: Search job postings
